# Browser game research and implementation decisions

Researched 26 October 2026. Links below are primary project or creator sources. Licenses are retained alongside bundled dependencies. No Undertale or Binding of Isaac artwork, music, characters, or maps are included.

## Chosen stack

**Buildless HTML + CSS + JavaScript modules + native Canvas.** This is the smallest useful stack for the current room-based adventure. It needs no build system, framework runtime, API keys, or game backend. A small Node server is supplied for local preview only. Static hosting serves the dist directory.

**CodeMirror 5.65.16**, vendored locally with its MIT license. Its C-like mode supports C++; the editor provides syntax highlighting, line numbers, indentation, undo, and keyboard entry. CodeMirror 6 is the better long-term modular option when a bundler and richer editor features are warranted. Primary references: [CodeMirror 5 manual](https://codemirror.net/5/doc/manual.html), [C-like mode source](https://github.com/codemirror/codemirror5/tree/master/mode/clike), [CodeMirror 6 basic setup](https://codemirror.net/examples/basic/). The prototype does not claim a language server, autocomplete, step debugger, or static type diagnostics in the editor.

**Compiler Explorer**, real remote GCC 14.1 with C++20. Its documented execution API accepts source and compiler options, returning build diagnostics, execution status, stdout, and stderr. A live smoke test confirmed execution and CORS access from an unrelated origin. Each Run submits a single compilation; multiple function checks share a generated driver. Explicit user opt-in is shown before submission. No request occurs on typing. `allowStoreCodeDebug` is false; this flag does not replace the service's privacy/operational policies. Reference: [official API](https://github.com/compiler-explorer/compiler-explorer/blob/main/docs/API.md).

**Local fonts:** Silkscreen for pixel headings and IBM Plex Mono for code and text, from the Google Fonts source repository. Both are distributed under the SIL Open Font License with the license files included. [Silkscreen source](https://github.com/google/fonts/tree/main/ofl/silkscreen), [IBM Plex Mono source](https://github.com/google/fonts/tree/main/ofl/ibmplexmono).

**Original Canvas pixel art and Web Audio.** All room tiles, player sprites, enemy variants, torches, terminals, particles, portraits, and small audio tones are drawn/generated by the app's own source. This keeps the prototype coherent and avoids asset dependencies. No raster generation was needed for code-native game sprites.

## Shortlist for expansion

| Resource | Useful role | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| [Phaser](https://docs.phaser.io/) | Mature 2D web engine with Canvas/WebGL, scenes, input, tilemaps, audio | Strong choice once there are many rooms, collision layers, or combat systems. Unnecessary runtime for this small prototype. |
| [Phaser installation](https://docs.phaser.io/phaser/getting-started/installation) | npm and CDN distribution | Prefer pinned npm version with a bundler for an expanded game. |
| [Tiled](https://www.mapeditor.org/) | Map editor with object layers and JSON export | Author room layouts and encounter triggers visually in production. |
| [Kenney Tiny Dungeon](https://kenney.nl/assets/tiny-dungeon) | 130 16×16 dungeon sprites, CC0 | Useful base for alternate rooms or placeholders. Researched, not bundled. |
| [Kenney's Tiny Dungeon itch page](https://kenney-assets.itch.io/tiny-dungeon) | Creator-hosted pack and licensing details | Confirms commercial use and attribution policy; credit remains good practice. |
| [CodeMirror 6](https://codemirror.net/) | Modular editor and language support | Upgrade for richer editor behavior and maintained modular integration. |
| [Compiler Explorer](https://github.com/compiler-explorer/compiler-explorer) | Compilation/execution service | Appropriate for a low-volume prototype. Production needs an owned isolated judge or an agreed service arrangement. |

## Art and interaction direction

Undertale informs intimate dialogue, readable silhouettes, moral stakes, quiet tension, and agency. The Binding of Isaac informs top-down room framing and compact encounters. This is an original digital dungeon: olive-charcoal masonry, amber electricity, cyan survivors, paperclips as discarded matter, and a coral eye guarding each stream. Coding is the encounter mechanic rather than an activity attached to an unrelated combat game.

## Compiler architecture tradeoff

A game written for the browser does not imply a C++ compiler written for the browser. Browser JavaScript runs the world; the player learns real C++ through the compiler service. A local WebAssembly C++ toolchain would remove the runtime network dependency, but substantially increases download size, worker/filesystem complexity, startup time, and debugging effort. A public execution API is the simplest verifiable prototype route.

The public service has no availability or throughput guarantee for this product. On network failure, compilation failure, timeout, or execution failure the app reports the condition, retains the draft, and does not grant progress. There is no fake compiler or keyword-only pass path.

For production, use an owned, strongly isolated judge with process-level CPU/memory/output limits, no outbound network, restricted filesystem, queued jobs, rate controls, dynamic server-side cases, and sanitizer support. Compiler Explorer's operational sandbox is external; this static app cannot configure its isolation or enforce a guaranteed memory limit. Frontend teaching-pattern checks are only nudges, not a secure validator.
